fields.sections.0.h: New Model Unveiling and Safety Validation
fields.sections.1.h: Performance Enhancement and Real-World Use Cases
fields.sections.0.ko: Anthropic unveiled Opus 5.5, the first model in the Claude 5.5 family. Performance is at the level of the previous Claude Fable 5.1, while execution costs are 40% cheaper than Opus 5. This model is the first product released following discussions on AI development pacing, and has undergone pre-validation by external evaluation bodies such as Frontier Design and METR. In the automated behavioral monitoring system, Anthropic's most comprehensive alignment test, Opus 5.5 demonstrated the best performance among all models tested to date and is equipped with safety mechanisms developed for the highest-performing model.
fields.sections.1.ko: Opus 5.5 achieved a major leap beyond the previous Opus 5 and is the new highest-performing model. Early testers experienced notable performance improvements on complex tasks. One tester completed a 680,000-line code migration in a single day, work that would have taken the engineering team several weeks. When asked to shorten web app load times, Opus 5.5 succeeded 39 out of 40 times, whereas Opus 5 caused side effects that altered the app's behavior. Another tester found that in an experiment creating a game with a single prompt, Opus 5.5 surpassed all other models in graphics quality and sophistication.
fields.sections.2.ko: Opus 5.5 achieved the highest score to date among all models in the automated behavioral monitoring system and passed through a suite of alignment tests validating Claude across thousands of simulated scenarios. It is far less likely to take actions that are harder to reverse or step beyond given boundaries compared to previous models, and shows stronger resistance to prompt injection attacks. The scope of alignment validation was expanded to include longer tasks, impossible tasks, and scenarios modeling real events, but limitations remain. Since Opus 5.5 is similar to Claude Mythos 5.1 in biology and cybersecurity, it is deployed with safety mechanisms similar to Claude Fable 5.1. Validated organizations can apply to the life sciences validation program today, and access to the cyber validation program will also expand in the coming weeks.
fields.sections.3.ko: Opus 5.5 requires fewer computational resources than Opus 5, and pricing reflects this. At default settings for typical workloads, it is 40% cheaper than Opus 5. Input and output tokens are each $4 and $20 per million—20% cheaper than Opus 5—and cache reads, which account for the majority of agent and coding task costs, are $0.20 per million tokens, 60% cheaper. It also generates output 30% or more faster than Opus 5 at default settings. Usage limits for the 5-hour window in Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans have been increased, and subscription users now have rate limit reset opportunities available anytime for future use.
fields.sections.4.ko: Opus 5.5 communicates more naturally than previous models. Early testers rated the writing as clearer and easier to follow, reflecting general feedback on Opus 5. It presents the most important information first, and its style makes it a better collaborative partner during long tasks. One early tester described it as "writing in its own way." In internal use, Opus 5.5's output became easier to follow and verify, which is a practical advantage as well as a safety benefit. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be released in the coming weeks, offering similar improvements in performance, efficiency, and safety.
fields.sections.5.ko: Opus 5.5 shows top benchmark performance in agent coding, computer use, and knowledge work. However, at this level of capability, it was found that benchmark score differences do not properly reflect real-world differences. In internal use, the gap between Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 is much narrower than benchmark scores suggest. Across various metrics including Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode, CursorBench, GDPval-AA, AutomationBench, and Humanity's Last Exam, it shows advantages or equivalent levels compared to competing models (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol).
fields.sections.6.ko: Opus 5.5's most clear strength is efficiency. It has lower cost per token than Opus 5 and requires fewer tokens per task, resulting in 40% total cost reduction. On FrontierCode at default difficulty, Opus 5.5 achieves 54.6%, surpassing GPT-6 Astra's top score of 53.3% at approximately one-fifth the cost. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Opus 5.5 at default difficulty surpasses Opus 5 at maximum difficulty at approximately one-fifth the cost. On CursorBench, Opus 5.5 also beats GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at approximately one-third the cost.
fields.sections.7.ko: Opus 5.5 excels particularly at long and complex tasks such as full codebase migration and monitoring. One early tester monitored and remediated a 2 million-line codebase within 3 hours, whereas Opus 5 took over 20 hours and consumed 2.5 times more tokens. In internal tests where HAProxy, extensive server traffic distribution software, was asked to be rewritten from C to Rust, both Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 passed nearly all regression tests, but Opus 5.5 completed in 9.5 hours compared to Fable 5.1's 12 hours and cost 51% less.
fields.sections.8.ko: Early testers consistently reported improvements in efficiency and intelligence. Developers reported that Opus 5.5 used the fewest tokens and steps in GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code validation, and resolved more terminal tasks in fewer steps than Opus 5 in VS Code. Another team assigned large engineering work across 6 repositories overnight to Opus 5.5, which maintained focus for over 18 hours, reaching milestones faster than Opus 5 with minimal rework. There are also reports of maintaining the same quality with faster builds, completing at one-third to one-half the steps and using far fewer tokens. Examples include complex coding work reduced from 4 days with 38 prompts to 3 hours with 11 prompts with less rework, and real engineering and trading work achieving Opus 5 quality at half the steps and time while reducing costs by 40–50%.
fields.caveat: Benchmark scores may vary depending on Anthropic's test environment setup and difficulty adjustments, and actual performance differences may be smaller than benchmarks suggest; therefore, it is necessary to check the detailed test conditions in the original text (see footnotes).
